opportunities.relevance_reason: Could be hosted by Fabian Hassler, Piet Brouwer, Felix von Oppen from your PI list.
opportunities.summary: There are no call windows. The DFG Walter Benjamin Programme takes proposals at any time through the elan portal, and a decision takes about 6 months on average. It funds early-career postdocs to carry out their own project, usually for up to two years. In Germany you hold a postdoc position at the host, normally paid at 100%, plus €250 a month for project, travel and publication costs. Abroad you get a fellowship instead (basic amount plus allowances). Carlos appears eligible for the German position, for example with Brouwer or von Oppen at FU Berlin or Hassler at RWTH Aachen: that track has no nationality or prior-Germany-work rules, and he would be changing institution from ICMM-CSIC. He can submit once his dissertation has been handed in (expected around early 2027, with proof of submission and a supervisor statement), but funding only starts after the doctorate is completed. That makes a start around late 2027 realistic. He is not eligible for the abroad fellowship (for example a stay in Copenhagen), because he has not been integrated into the German research system.
opportunities.eligibility: For postdocs in the early phase after the doctorate (EU 'recognised researcher', R2). DFG sets no fixed number of years since the PhD, and parental leave is taken into account. You can submit once the dissertation has been handed in, but funding starts only after the doctorate is completed. You must generally change institution (not the PhD institution or current one, except with special justification). You must not have worked more than one year at the chosen host when you submit. German position: no nationality or prior-Germany restrictions. Abroad fellowship: you need to have worked at least 3 continuous years in Germany just before the proposal, or have done most of your schooling and higher education in Germany with no more than 3 years abroad for research since the PhD. Carlos does not meet these. The host cannot be for-profit and must allow open publication.
opportunities.duration: As a rule up to 24 months. The German position and the abroad fellowship modules can be combined. In France, fellowships are limited to 12 months unless you move to a second French institution.
opportunities.salary: German position: a postdoc post ('postdoctoral researcher and comparable'), usually at 100%, plus €250 a month for direct project, travel and publication costs. The exact pay scale is not stated. Non-university institutes (Max Planck, Helmholtz, Fraunhofer) must guarantee 45% of the position's funding. Abroad fellowship: a monthly basic amount plus foreign, cost-of-living and travel allowances and benefits for children, paid directly to the fellow.

opportunities.relevance_reason: Could be hosted by Karsten Flensberg, Fabian Hassler, Piet Brouwer, Felix von Oppen… from your PI list.
opportunities.summary: No call is open today (2026-11-04). The 2026 call (HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01) ran from 9 April to 9 September 2026, with results due around February 2027. The next call, HORIZON-MSCA-2027-PF-01-01, is listed as forthcoming on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and the MSCA site: planned opening 7 April 2027, deadline 8 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. Some sources still mark these dates as provisional, so check the portal before relying on them. European Fellowships last 12–24 months at a host in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. They pay the researcher living, mobility and, where applicable, family allowances, and pay the host research, training, networking, management and indirect costs. The host PI/organisation writes the proposal with the fellow, submits it, and if funded employs and supervises the fellow. Carlos appears eligible for the 2027 call. His PhD (expected March 2027) would be awarded before the September 2027 deadline, he is well within the 8-year limit, and he has lived only in Spain. That means any host outside Spain (for example Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Italy, Sweden or Switzerland) meets the mobility rule. A Spanish host would not. Because his 2025 Copenhagen visit was short, Denmark should still be fine as a host. As an EU national he could also apply for a Global Fellowship to the US or Canada, which adds a mandatory 12-month return phase in Europe. Host institutions often set internal deadlines between April and July, so he should contact host PIs early in 2027.
opportunities.eligibility: Any nationality (European Fellowships). You need a PhD by the call deadline; a defended thesis counts even before the degree is formally awarded. You can have at most 8 years of research experience after the PhD; career breaks, work outside research, parental leave and long sick leave are not counted. Mobility rule: in the 36 months before the deadline, you must not have lived or had your main activity (work, studies) in the host country for more than 12 months. From 2026, a proposal that scored below 80% the year before cannot be resubmitted with the same host and researcher. Global Fellowships are open only to EU nationals or long-term residents.
opportunities.duration: 12–24 months (European Fellowships). Global Fellowships are 24–36 months: 12–24 months outside Europe plus a mandatory 12-month return phase. An optional non-academic placement of up to 6 months is possible at the end.
opportunities.salary: Unit-cost funding. The researcher receives a living allowance (adjusted by the host country's correction coefficient), a mobility allowance, and, where applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances; employer social security costs are included. The host receives research, training and networking costs plus management and indirect costs. The 2027 indicative budget is about €330M for European Fellowships and €58M for Global Fellowships. I couldn't confirm the exact monthly rates from official pages in this search; they are in the MSCA Work Programme 2026–2027.

opportunities.summary: The Junior Leader Incoming 2027 call opened on 1 July 2026 and closed on 23 September 2026 at 14:00 Spanish time. The foundation's Spanish page now marks it 'Cerrada' (closed). Shortlisting is due 12 January 2027, interviews 16–17 February 2027 and results 10 March 2027. Fellows start between 1 May and 31 December 2027. Dates for the next call (Incoming 2028) have not been announced. Based on past cycles, it should open around July 2027 and close in late September or early October 2027. The fellowship lasts up to 3 years and is worth up to €320,100 in total. That covers employment costs of up to €64,000 a year (minimum gross salary €47,000 a year) and €38,500 a year for research costs, plus family and mobility allowances. Carlos is NOT currently eligible, for two reasons. (1) His PhD is expected in March 2027, but the PhD must be at least 2 years old at the deadline, so the earliest call he could apply to is the one with a deadline around September 2029. (2) He has lived in Spain all his life, so he fails the Incoming mobility rule for Spanish hosts: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in Spain in the 3 years before the deadline. He could become eligible for a Spanish host, such as a Severo Ochoa or María de Maeztu centre, after about 2 or more years of postdoc work abroad. Alternatively, he could apply to a host in Portugal, because the mobility rule there is about time spent in Portugal, which he would meet once the PhD-age rule is satisfied. The sister 'Retaining' modality requires at least 12 months in Spain plus at least 6 months of research abroad, and has the same rule that the PhD must be 2–7 years old.
opportunities.eligibility: Any nationality. Incoming mobility rule: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in Spain in the 3 years before the deadline if the host is in Spain; the same rule applies to Portugal for Portuguese hosts. The project must be in a STEM field at an eligible accredited university or research centre in Spain or Portugal.
opportunities.salary: Up to €320,100 in total (2027 call). Employment costs up to €64,000 a year, with a minimum gross salary of €47,000 a year. Research costs of €38,500 a year, covering consumables, equipment, travel, conferences and staff. Family allowance of €1,200 a year per dependent child. Mobility allowance of €5,400 for researchers who relocate. These figures come from the 2027 call (20 fellowships per modality).

opportunities.title: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship (European Fellowship) hosted in the Quantum Tinkerer group, TU Delft
opportunities.institution: Kavli Institute of Nanoscience / QuTech, TU Delft
opportunities.relevance_reason: This is the group of a listed PI, and it works on exactly your topics (Majoranas, hybrid devices, Kwant transport), but there is no funded post at present, so the route is a self-funded MSCA application on a future call.
opportunities.summary: The Akhmerov/Wimmer Quantum Tinkerer group has no funded openings at the moment. Its join page invites postdoc applicants, including those applying for their own fellowships, to send a CV and a short research statement. The realistic route is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowship with Akhmerov as host. The next call has not been announced but is likely to open in spring 2027 with a deadline in early autumn, after Carlos's expected PhD date (March 2027).
opportunities.eligibility: Must hold a PhD by the call deadline; MSCA mobility rule (no more than 12 months' residence in the Netherlands in the previous 36 months) is met by the candidate. The 2026 call closed 2026-09-09; the 2027 call is not yet announced.

opportunities.title: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship (European Fellowship) hosted by Sapienza Università di Roma – van Heck group (next call, expected 2027)
opportunities.institution: Dipartimento di Fisica, Sapienza Università di Roma
opportunities.relevance_reason: Van Heck is on your PI list and works on Majorana zero modes, Andreev qubits and mesoscopic superconductivity, which closely matches your work, and you appear eligible for the MSCA call after your PhD; the score is not higher because this is a fellowship you would need to win, not a funded opening, and the 2027 dates are not yet published.
opportunities.summary: This is an independent EU Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowship that you would write yourself, with Bernard van Heck as host supervisor at Sapienza. The 2026 call closed on 2026-09-09. Recent calls have opened in April with deadlines in September, so the next one probably opens around April 2027, but the dates are not confirmed. To apply with Sapienza as host, email the International Research Office (ricercainternazionale@uniroma1.it) a self-declaration of eligibility, a letter of acceptance signed by the supervisor and your academic CV. The office pre-screens proposals and helps with writing, and Sapienza also runs an MSCA infoday and a grant-writing lab each spring.
opportunities.eligibility: MSCA PF European Fellowship rules: you must hold a PhD by the call deadline and have at most 8 years of post-PhD experience. You must not have lived or worked mainly in Italy for more than 12 months in the 36 months before the deadline. As a Spanish resident with a PhD expected in 2027-03, you meet these rules for a call with its deadline in September 2027.

opportunities.title: Postdoc on the theory of Si and Ge spin qubits
opportunities.institution: CEA Grenoble / IRIG (Interdisciplinary Research Institute of Grenoble), L_Sim
opportunities.relevance_reason: A theory post on solid-state qubits that uses large-scale tight-binding modelling alongside experimental groups, but on semiconductor spin qubits rather than your core Majorana and hybrid-nanowire topics; the April 2027 latest start is tight for a March 2027 PhD.
opportunities.summary: Two-year theory postdoc on modelling Si/SiGe and Ge spin qubits (spin manipulation and readout, exchange interactions in arrays, noise and disorder), using the in-house tight-binding code TB_Sim, in close collaboration with Grenoble's experimental groups. The post is open until filled, and the start must be no later than 1 April 2027. To apply, email Yann-Michel Niquet (yniquet@cea.fr) a CV, a publication list and a motivation letter, and arrange for two recommendation letters to be sent to him.
opportunities.eligibility: PhD in quantum, condensed matter or solid-state physics (or related field).

opportunities.title: ML4Q Postdoctoral Fellowship (Cluster of Excellence Matter and Light for Quantum Computing) – host: Hassler group, RWTH Aachen
opportunities.institution: Cluster of Excellence ML4Q (Universities of Cologne, Bonn, RWTH Aachen, HHU Düsseldorf, FZ Jülich); host: Institute for Quantum Information, RWTH Aachen
opportunities.relevance_reason: This prestigious independent fellowship could be held in Hassler's Majorana/mesoscopics theory group, and the autumn-2027 start fits your expected March 2027 PhD. Ask ML4Q whether you can apply before defending, since that is still unclear.
opportunities.summary: This independent 2-year fellowship pays for the fellow's own position plus consumables and travel, and includes training and mentoring, in an ML4Q group such as Hassler's at RWTH Aachen. The start date is autumn 2027 at the earliest. Up to two fellows are chosen per call. Email one PDF to ml4q-office@uni-koeln.de by 2026-12-14. It must contain a research statement (≤3 pages), a statement on links to the cluster (≤0.5 page), a CV (≤2 pages), a publication list, two referees and the name of the host group. The host must have discussed the application with you beforehand.
opportunities.eligibility: Usually no more than 4 years since your PhD, with allowance for career breaks. You must agree on a host ML4Q group before applying. Not open to current or recent (within 3 years) ML4Q group members, or to anyone whose current or former (co-)supervisor is an ML4Q member.
